chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: After-hours jam spots in New York
summary: Basement and speakeasy spots by instrument night, Mexico's, the 101 Ranch, the Elks and the Rhythm Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Eddie Durham wanted to beat up all those guys. But these are the little kind of tricks that guys used to play on one another, you know. Like -- and around New York especially, you know. But all the cities had it. It was going on in all the cities. But there were places around New York, them guys had little basements. They used to sell liquor. It wasn't -- it was illegal, you know. And they'd have certain nights, certain instruments play. Like maybe one night it would be nothing but pianos. Piano players.
Like at Mexico's in New York?
Yeah, this is the way it used to be way back. But they had several spots like that around.
Oh, really, where? I only know about Mexico's, Maxico's.

There was one on 131st Street, and there was the 101 Ranch. They used to have shows there but after they shows they just -- there were a lot of little spots. Over at the Elks Club on Lenox Avenue, there was several little clubs used to do it. One night there wouldn't be nothing but

tap dancers over there, dancing against one another, you know. There was all kind of different things they had going, you know. Whoever was in town, you know, they would get together. Sometimes you'd go by some guy's apartment that had a piano, and you just get in there and jam, you know. A lot of them are private that nobody even know but the guys who were playing about them -- knew about this. But Mexico, yeah he had his place. Maxie (inaudible).

And then there was the Rythmn Club there. A lot of guys, all the musicians used to hang out around there. If a top act would come in town -- well, everybody's laying for them, you know. Yeah, these things happened all over New York, and they used to have them all over Chicago.
